pairs.why: A's spur sits on a proper strap around the heel, but B's spur sticks straight out of the heel with no strap, and B's shaft is a stiff, oddly long tube.
B's checkerboard has a regular, believable grid, while A's board has too many squares that warp toward the far edge; the pedestals and stools are equally sound in both.
B's life ring hangs from a real hook on the post, but A's ring seems to float against the post, held only by a loose rope from the coil.
A is a wall clock mounted flat, but B's round clock stands on its rim on the floor with no foot or stand, so it would roll.
B's keypad has a working layout of digits and operators, but A's 16 keys have no labels, so the calculator could not be used.
A's cat has normal anatomy with the tail joined at the rump, while B's head sits stiffly on a collar ring and its tail is a blob wrapped around the front.
A's life ring hangs from a peg on the post by a rope loop, but B's ring hangs loosely mid-pier and its reflection floats on open water far from the dock.
The two wagons are nearly identical in wheel count, axles, canvas hoops and tongue, so neither shows a clear construction difference.
